messages:
Marta G: FYI - customer hit schema validation errors from our toolcall endpoint. They say args are being cut off mid-JSON when using streaming. Example error: "InvalidToolArgs: unexpected end of JSON input"

Ryan M: Can you paste the raw stream payload they received? any proxy in front?

Customer Support: Pasting the snippet they attached. Note the trailing partial JSON in the last chunk:

Customer: [stream start]
data: {"type":"tool_call","name":"create_charge","args":{"amount":1999,"currency":"usd","metadata":{"order_id":"ORD-123"}}}
data: {"type":"tool_call","name":"confirm_charge","args":{"charge_id":"ch_1A2B3C","confirm":true}}
data: {"type":"tool_call","name":"notify_customer","args":{"email":"user@example.com","template":"receipt","items":["widget","gizmo"]}}
data: {"type":"tool_call","name":"capture_fraud","args":{"score":0.02,"details":{"source":"ml_detector"},"thresholds":{"warn":0.1,"block":0.9}}
[STREAM CUT OFF]

Marta G: You can see the last event ends mid-object (no closing braces). The runtime then tried to parse it and failed. The customer saw our 400 schema error. They are on a managed proxy in front of us (some CDN/edge).

Devon S: Important: does the runtime send each JSON as a single SSE event? We expect each event to be self-contained. If a proxy splits TCP chunks, SSE framing should still deliver full events. But if we flush partial bytes and the proxy re-chunks, some gateways may cut events.

Ryan M: Repro steps request from eng: 1) Use the streaming endpoint with a tool-enabled model. 2) Send a prompt leading to multiple consecutive tool calls. 3) Pipe through nginx reverse proxy with proxy_buffering off and chunk_size = 8192. 4) Observe final SSE event truncated.

Devon S: Customer reported they're behind CloudEdge (3rd-party). I suspect edge closes connection mid-stream on idle and the last chunk gets lost. We need logs showing connection close codes and our runtime's last write.

SRE Oncall: From infra logs (redacted):

[runtime] 2026-11-04T18:24:12.123Z INFO streaming: wrote 1423 bytes to socket
[runtime] 2026-11-04T18:24:12.124Z INFO streaming: wrote 312 bytes to socket
[proxy] 2026-11-04T18:24:12.200Z WARN connection: upstream reset by peer

SRE Oncall: Looks like upstream reset happens ~75ms after final write. If proxy cuts the stream during TCP close, last write may not reach client.

Ryan M: Temporary mitigation: in the SDK we can send a trailing sentinel event after every tool_call, e.g. data: {"__end_of_event":true}
That would let parsers ignore incomplete payloads until sentinel appears. But it's a client-side parsing change.

Marta G: Customer needs a quicker workaround. Any gateway config we can change?

Devon S: Suggestion for infra: set keepalive_timeout higher and ensure proxy waits for upstream flush before closing; also set proxy_buffering on so proxy buffers full SSE events. If using CloudEdge ask them to disable connection preemption for streaming routes.

infra-bot: Ticket created: INFRA-3241 - Investigate SSE truncation for streaming toolcalls (linked to cust-8872). Assigned to Devon S.

Customer Support: Customer wants repro steps so they can test a fix on their side. Ryan — can you provide a minimal curl example we can share?

Ryan M: Minimal reproduce (dev):

```bash
# consumer side
curl -N -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" \
  -d '\{"model":"tool-v1","prompt":"multi tool calls"\}' \
  https://api.redwood.example/v1/stream

# proxy side (nginx snippet)
location /v1/stream {
  proxy_pass http://upstream_runtime;
  proxy_buffering off;  # toggling this reproduces different behaviors
  proxy_http_version 1.1;
  chunked_transfer_encoding on;
}
```

Ryan M: If they see truncated JSON, have them toggle proxy_buffering and chunked_transfer_encoding. Also try adding Content-Length on server side for non-streaming tests.

Marta G: Action items:
- Devon: confirm if runtime v0.9.3 has any recent fixes for event framing (ETA EOD).
- Infra: check gateway keepalive/close semantics for streaming routes (INFRA-3241).
- Support: give customer the curl snippet + ask them to try with buffering on/off and report back (I can offer a temporary bypass to route around CDN).

Ryan M: One more note: we should harden our server-side parser to be tolerant of partial last-event and log raw bytes for every parse failure (include connection id). That will speed future triage.

Devon S: Agreed. I will add debug logging behind a flag to avoid noise.

Customer Support: Thanks—I'll relay and update the ticket when they test. :thumbsup:
